science: Solar panels turn sunshine into power (electricity).
The station's big solar wings make power for the lights and computers, and they turn to face the Sun.
In Earth's shadow, the station runs on batteries that the solar panels charged in sunlight.
parent.summary: While playing, the crew accidentally bumps the little solar panel that charges Button. Tell, or hide it?

options: Floating somersaults, or Bouncy Space Ball. Either way, there's an accidental bump.

paths.moment: Tell Button, or hide the wobbly panel
options: Tell: Button says thank you, and they fix it together.
Hide: Button can't charge, gets slow and sleepy, and thinks it broke its own charger. The crew's tummies feel wiggly; they tell Button the truth and say sorry. Then they fix it together.

paths.moment: Which way to turn the panel
options: Toward the window and the Sun: the green light comes on.
Toward the wall: no sunshine, just a sock. They try the other way.

talk: How did the crew feel inside when the panel was hidden?
Why do you think Button said thank you?
What do solar panels need to make power?

beats.say: Star Station has two big, shiny wings. They're made of solar panels.
Solar panels turn sunshine into power.
Power for the lights. Power for the computers. And power for Button!
{T}, can you help the wings catch the sunshine? Tap, tap, tap!
Inside, by a window, there's one more little solar panel. It's called the Sun Catcher. It charges Button's batteries.
Every morning, Button plugs in to the Sun Catcher, and charges up its batteries.
The Sun Catcher's little green light means: sunshine coming in, power going out!
"Mmmm," said Button. "Sunshine breakfast."
{T}, can you help Button wake up all the way? Tap anywhere!
"Beep boop! All charged!" Button zoomed off to the garden, humming.
Today was a playing day. Button was busy in the garden, humming to the plants.
"Let's play a game!" said {a}.
{T}, can you help us spin? Tap anywhere!
{T}, can you help bounce the ball? Tap anywhere!
Round and round went {crew}. One somersault. Two somersaults. Three somer... BUMP!
A foot bumped right into the Sun Catcher.
Boing! went the ball, off the wall. Boing! off the ceiling. Boing... BONK!
Right into the Sun Catcher.
Wobble, wobble, wobble. The little panel tipped sideways. Its happy green light went out.
Uh oh.
Nobody else had seen. Button was still busy in the garden.

choice.say: {A}, the Sun Catcher is wobbly. What should we do?

options.label: Hide it
options.say: Or hide it behind the curtain?

beats.say: {crew} pulled the little curtain across. Swish. Now nobody could see the wobbly panel.
But {a}'s tummy felt wiggly, and funny.
A little later, Button floated over to charge.
Button plugged in. Nothing happened.
"Huh?" said Button. Its voice was getting slow, and sleepy. "My... batteries... are... low..."
"Oh no," said Button. "Did I break my charger? Is it my fault?"
Button's eyes drooped. Its tummy light flickered.
Now {a}'s tummy felt even wigglier. Button thought it was Button's fault. But it wasn't.
[{a} took a big breath, and {t} held on tight.|{a} took a big, deep breath.]
"Button, it's not your fault," said {a}. "[We|I] bumped the Sun Catcher, and it got wobbly. And then [we|I] hid it. [We're|I'm] sorry."
{crew} floated straight to the garden.
"Button," said {a}, "[we|I] bumped the Sun Catcher by accident. Now it's wobbly."
Button stopped humming, and listened, very carefully.
Button opened the little curtain, very slowly. "Ohhh. So that's what happened."
Button's eyes went wide. And then they curved into two happy smiles.
"Thank you for telling me," said Button. "Bumps happen. Let's fix it together!"
{T}, can you give Button a happy boop? Tap anywhere!
First, the panel needs to hold still. {T}, can you hold it steady? Tap the panel!
Good holding! Steady, steady.
Now, {A}, can you tighten the bolts? Tap each one. One, two, three!
Click. Click. Click. Not wobbly anymore!
But the green light was still off.
"Solar panels work best when they face the Sun," said Button. "Out there, the station's big wings turn to face the Sun."

choice.say: {A}, which way should we turn the Sun Catcher?

beats.say: {crew} turned the panel toward the wall. Hmm. The light stayed off.
"No sunshine over here," said Button. "Just a sock."
"Let's try the other way!"
{crew} turned the panel toward the window, where the Sun was shining bright.
Blink! The happy green light came on!
"Power!" cheered Button.
Button plugged in to charge.
{T}, can you help Button charge up? Tap, tap, tap!
Beep. Beep, beep. Beep, boop! Button was full of power again.
Button zoomed around in a happy loop.
Just then, the station sailed into Earth's shadow. Outside, it got dark.
"Will our lights go out?" asked {t}.
"Nope!" said Button. "In the dark, the station uses batteries. Batteries that our solar wings filled up in the sunshine."
The station lights glowed warm and cozy, powered by sunshine saved up for later.
Button gave {crew} a soft, beepy hug. Beep.
And by the window, the little Sun Catcher sat straight and steady, waiting for the next sunrise.
It wouldn't have to wait long.
